AD.title: Institutional and health progress, with gaps in protection and care capacity.
AD.summary: ILGA-Europe brings improvements in trans healthcare and harassment prevention, but also hate incidents, lack of clear public protection for intersex bodily integrity and tensions with civil society.
AD.legal_context: In October, the decree on specific health care for trans persons, with hormonal therapy coverage since the age of 16 and gender-assertive surgery since the age of 18, entered into force. Companies must have protocols to deal with sexual and gender-based harassment.
AD.social_context: The police reported incidents motivated by prejudice on a regular basis; civil organizations called for a formal system of recording hate crimes and reported a lack of training and specialized resources in trans healthcare.
AD.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 26-27 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: The framework for trans healthcare and public treatment coverage is in force.
Implementation of business protocols against sexual and gender-based harassment.
main_challenges: Adopt public and transparent guarantees of the bodily integrity of intersex minors.
Improve the registration of LGBTIQ+-phobic violence and the training of health professionals.

AL.title: Relevant policy developments, but with persistent discrimination and institutional mistrust.
AL.summary: The country expanded formal protections during 2025, while ILGA-Europe documentation reflects that the LGBTIQ+ population continues to face violence, exclusion from work and difficulties in exercising rights in practice.
AL.legal_context: In November, Parliament adopted the "On Gender Equality" law, aligning the legal definition of gender with the Istanbul Convention and explicitly extending protection against discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression. There are still shortcomings in the recognition of same-sex couples and the legal recognition of gender.
AL.social_context: The surveys and cases cited above show high levels of discrimination, violence and mistrust towards institutions, along with campaigns to disinform and stigmatize LGBTIQ+ people and activists.
AL.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 21-25 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Adoption of an equality law with explicit protection for sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression.
Acceptance of international recommendations on same-sex couples, hate crimes and intersex interventions.
main_challenges: Effective implementation of anti-discrimination guarantees and improved confidence in police and justice.
Reduce violence, exclusion from work and barriers that especially affect trans and non-binary people.

AM.title: A fragile environment, with insufficient protection from violence and discrimination.
AM.summary: The report documents discrimination in employment, violence - including domestic violence - and an institutional response still limited, especially in hate, trans healthcare and hate crimes and legal gender recognition.
AM.legal_context: Armenia lacks a comprehensive framework for legal gender recognition and gender-affirming healthcare. The State gender policy strategy 2025-2028 was considered an institutional step, although it does not explicitly incorporate sexual orientation and gender identity as protected grounds.
AM.social_context: Domestic violence, harassment, labour discrimination and difficulties for authorities to recognize anti-LGBTIQ+ bias as an aggravating circumstance persist.
AM.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 28-32 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Adoption of a State gender policy strategy 2025-2028.
The Office of the Ombudsman is more involved and the EU-Armenia cooperation framework in human rights is further developed.
main_challenges: Create explicit legal protection and effective procedures for legal gender recognition and trans healthcare.
Improve the investigation of hate crimes and protection against family, labour and social violence.

AT.title: Comprehensive protections and new legal developments, with challenges for intersex and non-binary people.
AT.summary: Austria recorded favourable court decisions and reforms concerning family recognition, identity documents and healthcare, although hate-motivated attacks continued and policy gaps persisted.
AT.legal_context: The recognition of same-sex marriages in cross-border situations was strengthened and a neutral gender passport was issued after European case law, a ruling recognized the health coverage of laser waxing for a trans woman.
AT.social_context: Hate-motivated attacks were documented and the debate on the protection of intersex persons and the recognition of non-binary identities continued.
AT.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (pp. 33-35 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Reform to recognize same-sex marriages in international contexts.
Progress in documentary recognition and health coverage for trans persons.
main_challenges: To establish a general legal recognition procedure for non-binary persons.
To prohibit medically unnecessary and unconsensual interventions on intersex minors and to continue to combat hate violence.

AZ.title: A highly restrictive environment with serious risks of institutional abuse.
AZ.summary: The review describes political and social hostility towards LGBTIQ+ people, police operations against queer spaces and reports of violence, extortion and lack of institutional transparency.
AZ.legal_context: The framework described above does not provide sufficient effective protection against discrimination and violence. The authorities did not provide transparent explanations in several police proceedings directed against LGBTIQ+ persons or spaces.
AZ.social_context: Trans people and gay men in detention were described as especially exposed to isolation and violence; the community reported fear, extortion and reduction of safe spaces.
AZ.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF, pp. 36-37). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Civil society and community media continued to document abuses and make the situation visible.
The international review has a focus on police practices and the protection of fundamental rights.
main_challenges: Ensure independent investigations into police abuse and end extortion and violence against LGBTIQ+ persons.
To establish effective guarantees of non-discrimination, freedom of expression and freedom of assembly.

BA.title: Partial progress in recognition and visibility, but with incomplete family rights and practical protection.
BA.summary: During 2025, there were steps in the area of same-sex couples, legal gender recognition and hate crime management, while hostile attacks and discourses continued.
BA.legal_context: The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina reactivated a working group on a law on same-sex couples, and a court in Sarajevo ruled in favour of a trans woman whose legal recognition had been conditional on divorce.
BA.social_context: Sarajevo Pride brought together about a thousand people, but subsequent attacks and social and institutional obstacles persisted, including local public funding for anti-LGBTIQ+ groups.
BA.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 45-46 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Reactivation of legislative work on same-sex couples.
A court decision in favour of a transgender person and improvements in systems for the registration of hate crimes.
main_challenges: Adopt an effective framework for the recognition of couples and ensure their implementation.
Combating violence, hate speech and public funding of discriminatory initiatives.

BE.title: A sound legal and institutional framework, although with a more polarized social climate.
BE.summary: Belgium maintains comprehensive equality policies and a legal gender recognition procedure based on self-determination, while the 2025 data and cases show that violence and discrimination remain present.
BE.legal_context: The institutions strengthened labour inclusion guides and diversity criteria; the administrative procedure for changing the scoreboard recorded a record number of applications; there were also decisions against discriminatory requirements affecting trans women.
BE.social_context: The studies mentioned above identify greater exposure to violence, discrimination and avoidance behaviour, along with barriers in housing, family and access to services for certain groups.
BE.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF 41-44). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: New job inclusion tools for intersex, trans and non-binary people.
The continued and increasing use of the legal gender recognition procedure based on self-determination.
main_challenges: Reduce violence and social discrimination despite formal protections.
Ensure that new measures on associations and security do not disproportionately erode civic space.

BG.title: Retreat in education and trans recognition, with violence and little state response.
BG.summary: The prohibition of LGBTIQ+ content in schools deepened the fear in the educational field and the absence of an effective procedure for the legal recognition of gender persists.
BG.legal_context: The country still does not offer a quick, transparent and accessible procedure for legal recognition of gender despite European convictions.
BG.social_context: Serious attacks on trans people and a climate of disinformation were documented; civil organizations expanded medical networks and health support in the face of inadequate public services.
BG.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 47-48 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: European litigation is putting pressure on the country to remove barriers to legal gender recognition.
The European dispute is under pressure to correct barriers to legal gender recognition.
main_challenges: Reverse educational restrictions that exclude LGBTIQ+ content.
Establish effective legal gender recognition and improve the prevention and investigation of anti-LGBTIQ+ violence.

BY.title: Serious backwardness, with state repression and increasing criminalization of LGBTIQ+ space.
BY.summary: ILGA-Europe describes an intensification of pressure through "propaganda" standards, designations of extremism, surveillance and police actions against people, activists and queer spaces.
BY.legal_context: Restrictions were tightened on information on homosexuality and gender transition, and human rights organizations or media were designated as "extremists." The gender recognition procedure continued to be subject to a restrictive State commission.
BY.social_context: Detentions, interrogations, doxing, raids and pressure on relatives of LGBTIQ+ who had left the country were documented.
BY.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 38-40 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: There continued to be an administrative route for some requests for trans healthcare and legal recognition, although with strong limitations.
The documentation of human rights organizations continued to record abuses despite the repressive context.
main_challenges: Stop police persecution and extremist designations directed against activism and LGBTIQ+ media.
Eliminate "propaganda" restrictions and ensure accessible and human rights-friendly gender recognition procedures.

CH.title: High social support for LGBTIQ+ rights, but with a sharp increase in hate incidents.
CH.summary: Public opinion is broadly supportive of equality, while community records show a very sharp rise in attacks and discrimination, especially against trans people.
CH.legal_context: Cantons made progress in initiatives to prohibit conversion practices and the ECHR issued a relevant judgement in the Semenya case on discrimination and due process.
CH.social_context: The LGBTI Helpline report recorded 309 incidents in 2024 and a strong increase since 2020; at the same time, surveys show majority support for rights and protections.
CH.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 156-156 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: High citizen support for LGBTIQ+ rights and anti-discrimination measures.
Progress of cantonal initiatives against conversion practices.
main_challenges: To respond to the rapid growth of attacks and discrimination, especially against trans persons.
Develop more uniform national protection against conversion practices and other violations.

CY.title: Mixed situation, with visibility and some protection mechanisms, but legal gaps and episodes of hostility.
CY.summary: The review covers legislative debates with a potential impact on trans people, problems with family recognition and shortcomings in responses to hate speech and hate-motivated incidents.
CY.legal_context: A project to legally define "women" and "gender" generated warnings that it could exclude women from existing protections. Administrative problems for same-sex families were also documented.
CY.social_context: There were attacks and altercations linked to Pride events, while initiatives such as United by Pride maintained a strong public presence and community-to-community coexistence.
CY.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 51-52 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Continuity of Pride events and greater public visibility of the community.
Institutional and judicial statements that emphasize the obligation to respond to anti-LGBTIQ+ hatred.
main_challenges: Avoid legal definitions that reduce the protection of trans persons.
Improve police response to hatred and resolve administrative barriers for families and LGBTIQ+ health care.

CZ.title: Important progress in legal gender recognition, although limits on family equality and political pressure persist.
CZ.summary: During 2025, the requirement for surgery or hormonal treatment to change the legal gender was eliminated in practice, while same-sex couples obtained more rights without achieving full marriage equality.
CZ.legal_context: Since July, a methodology of the Ministry of Health has allowed for the legal recognition of gender without surgery or hormonal treatment, following constitutional and ECHR decisions. New rules of "partnership" with extended rights, but without full equal marriage and with restrictions on adoption, have entered into force.
CZ.social_context: The education and civil organization debate shows political polarization, while trans visibility increased in the media and public debate.
CZ.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (pp. 53-54 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Elimination of surgery / sterilization as a practical condition for legal gender recognition.
Expansion of the rights of same-sex couples through the reform of partnerships.
main_challenges: Complete a gender recognition procedure based on self-determination and without unnecessary medical burdens.
Close remaining differences in family rights and protect inclusive education from stigmatization campaigns.

DE.title: Relevant rights framework, but with a strong increase in violence and open legislative debates.
DE.summary: Germany made progress through constitutional proposals and family-law reforms, while offences motivated by prejudice related to sexual orientation and gender diversity reached worrying levels.
DE.legal_context: The Bundesrat initiated a process to strengthen the constitutional non-discrimination clause and the Ministry of Justice presented a reform of the right of filiation for various families, and the courts questioned the inequality of automatic recognition among families with two mothers.
DE.social_context: Federal statistics showed strong increases in crimes motivated by sexual orientation and gender diversity, with a prominent presence of right-wing extremism.
DE.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 70-72 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: The promotion of strengthening constitutional protection against discrimination.
Reforms and disputes aimed at equalizing parental recognition of same-sex families.
main_challenges: To respond to the increase in anti-LGBTIQ+ violence through coordinated and transparent measures.
Complete the filiation reforms and ensure inclusive policies in education and administration.

DK.title: Consolidated protections and new public policies, with discrimination and violence still present.
DK.summary: Denmark announced new investments and LGBTIQ+ action plans, along with regional health initiatives and inclusion policies, although the report notes that welfare gaps and hate crimes persist.
DK.legal_context: The Government allocated funds to a new LGBTIQ+ 2026-2029 plan and rejected proposals that would have reduced the health autonomy of young trans. Regional policies were developed to improve health care.
DK.social_context: The public debate includes polarized gender discourse, while parties and institutions recognize the need to address discrimination, violence and differences in well-being.
DK.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 55-57 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: LGBTIQ+ Action Plan 2026-2029 with specific funding.
Development of regional and municipal policies to improve inclusion and health care.
main_challenges: Reduce hate crimes and well-being inequalities outside the large urban areas.
To move forward in guarantees for intersex persons and in a sustained response to discrimination.

EE.title: A favourable approach to a new comprehensive national LGBTIQ+ equality plan.
EE.summary: Estonia strengthened institutional support and adopted an action plan covering education, health, employment, justice, hate crimes and protection of intersex persons.
EE.legal_context: A national plan with planned reforms was adopted in December to expand anti-discrimination protection, review gender marker procedures and improve the protection of intersex minors.
EE.social_context: The Government expressed visible support for LGBTIQ+ rights in Tallinn Pride, IDAHOBIT and foreign policy, and provides training for schools, workplaces, police and prisons.
EE.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 58-58 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Adoption of a comprehensive national plan for equality and protection of LGBTIQ+.
Specific commitments in education, health, employment, justice and foreign policy.
main_challenges: Convert the plan's commitments to reforms and measurable results.
Ensure the effective implementation of new guarantees against discrimination and hate crimes.

ES.title: Advanced legal framework and institutional resistance to setbacks, with discrimination and violence still significant.
ES.summary: Spain maintains a broad equality framework, but 2025 saw regional attempts to weaken LGBTIQ+ legislation, numerous hate crimes and instances of hate speech, and discrimination in education and services.
ES.legal_context: A number of institutions and courts applied equality laws against discrimination and aggression. The Canary Islands rejected the repeal of equality laws and Catalonia passed Law 13/2025, strengthening sanctions against LGBTIQ+-phobia, conversion practices and online incitement.
ES.social_context: Convictions for homophobic abuse, assault and discrimination were documented, in addition to a report by FELGTBI + that more than half of the LGBTIQ+ students surveyed had suffered hatred or discrimination in secondary school.
ES.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (pp. 145-151 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Institutional rejection of attempts to repeal equality laws in the Canary Islands.
New Catalan legislation that reinforces sanctions against LGBTIQ+-phobia, conversion practices and online incitement.
main_challenges: Reduce hate and discrimination crimes, especially in education and public spaces.
Avoid self-government setbacks and ensure a uniform application of equality laws throughout the territory.

FI.title: Relevant protections, but with increased hate crimes and pending reforms.
FI.summary: The country recorded record numbers of hate crimes and numerous incidents against Pride events, while a parliamentary initiative to ban conversion practices was stalled.
FI.legal_context: Parliament supported a citizens' initiative to ban conversion practices, but the Government did not submit legislation to implement it during 2025.
FI.social_context: Police data showed an increase in hate crimes and the investigation by Seta indicated that a high proportion of Pride events were harassed or punished.
FI.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 59-60 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: I am very much in favour of the ban on conversion practices.
First court sentence in a case involving conversion practices treated as psychological violence.
main_challenges: Transform political support into an effective legal ban on conversion practices.
Brake the growth of hate crimes and improve the safety of LGBTIQ+ events and people.

FR.title: Comprehensive rights framework, accompanied by persistent violence and discrimination.
FR.summary: The review documents judicial and institutional actions against discrimination and attacks, as well as historical memory measures, but also numerous cases of violence, harassment and difficulties in schools and services.
FR.legal_context: There were court decisions on asylum, health access and discrimination, and the Senate had adopted an initiative to rehabilitate persons convicted under old standards that criminalized homosexuality.
FR.social_context: There were multiple ambushes and attacks through dating applications, in addition to an increase in serious incidents in educational facilities and cases of lesbophobic and transphobic harassment.
FR.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 61-65 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Progress in institutional recognition of victims of former discriminatory laws.
Judicial and administrative actions against discrimination in health, asylum and services.
main_challenges: Reduce anti-LGBTIQ+ violence and ambushes organized through applications.
Strengthen the prevention of harassment and discrimination in education and public services.

GB.title: A very controversial legal environment, with setbacks and high uncertainty for trans people.
GB.summary: The Supreme Court's ruling on the meaning of "sex" in the Equality Act brought about changes and disputes about access to single-sex spaces and services, while intensive discussions were held on health, education and trans recognition.
GB.legal_context: Following the Supreme Court's ruling, EHRC issued guidelines linking access to single-sex services to biological sex, leading to judicial challenges and revision of codes of practice, and the framework for legal recognition of gender remained under strong controversy.
GB.social_context: High levels of speech and hate crime were maintained, and policies on transgender persons generated strong polarization in services, education and health.
GB.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (pp. 171-177 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Judicial control of new guidelines on single-sex services and broad public debate on their compatibility with human rights.
The availability of up-to-date data on hate crimes, which can measure the evolution of violence and discrimination.
main_challenges: Clarify the impact of case law on the daily rights of trans persons without generating disproportionate exclusion.
Reduce hate crime and speech and ensure human rights-friendly health and educational policies.

GE.title: Severe regression and a shrinking civic space for LGBTIQ+ people and organisations.
GE.summary: Following the anti-LGBTIQ+ legislation adopted in 2025, legal, administrative and financing restrictions affecting organizations, public expression and gender recognition were consolidated during 2025.
GE.legal_context: "Gender identity" was eliminated from certain legal protections and monitoring mechanisms were strengthened for organizations financed from abroad, and the regulatory framework limits visibility, assembly and rights of trans people.
GE.social_context: Civil society describes loss of trust in institutions, pressure on organizations, stigmatization campaigns and demands for new marches and LGBTIQ+ symbols.
GE.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (pp. 66-69 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Civil society continued to document impacts and defend rights despite restrictions.
International attention to democratic and rights regression maintains external monitoring mechanisms.
main_challenges: Reverse legislation that restricts LGBTIQ+ rights and restore gender identity protections.
To guarantee freedom of association, financing, expression and assembly for organizations and activists.

GR.title: Important family developments, along with restrictions and barriers in health and trans rights.
GR.summary: Marriage equality, adopted in 2024, received constitutional support. However, restrictions on access to surrogacy were introduced in 2025, and administrative and healthcare barriers for trans people were documented.
GR.legal_context: The State Council confirmed the constitutionality of same-sex marriage and the associated adoption, but the Government restricted subrogated pregnancy for same-sex male and single-male couples.
GR.social_context: There were homophobic attacks and health access problems arising from administrative systems that do not adequately address the needs of trans persons.
GR.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 73-74 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Judicial confirmation of the constitutionality of equal marriage and the rights of adoption associated with it.
Application of homophobic-motivated aggravating measures in convictions for violence.
main_challenges: Eliminate administrative barriers in documents and health care for trans persons.
Review family restrictions and ensure evidence-based and non-discrimination-based blood and health policies.

HR.title: Moderate legal protection with judicial and local advances, but violence and persistent structural barriers.
HR.summary: Constitutional court rulings and local policy decisions strengthened equality, although organised attacks increased and legal gender recognition remains a challenge.
HR.legal_context: The courts acted in cases of discrimination and homophobic attacks; Zagreb maintains a local LGBTIQ+ equality programme until 2026. European bodies noted that legal gender recognition continues to be over-medicalized.
HR.social_context: Zagreb Pride warned of attacks organized through dating applications and the persistence of prejudice and discrimination.
HR.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 49-50 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Judicial decisions recognizing discrimination and State obligations in cases of violence.
The LGBTIQ+ equality programme of Zagreb city and local progress in public policy.
main_challenges: Reform legal gender recognition to make it less medicalized.
Respond effectively to organized attacks and anti-LGBTIQ+ discourse.

HU.title: Very serious backwardness in public freedoms and recognition of gender diversity.
HU.summary: During 2025, constitutional and legislative changes were adopted that facilitated the prohibition of LGBTIQ+ acts such as Pride, reinforced a binary conception of sex and reduced explicit protections.
HU.legal_context: The Constitution was amended to state that human beings are "men or women" and to prioritize arguments of child protection against certain freedoms of assembly; gender identity was removed from the explicit list of protected grounds of the equality law. In parallel, the Constitutional Court required the recognition of same-sex marriages held abroad as registered couples.
HU.social_context: Budapest Pride and other public expressions were subject to restrictions, sanctions and institutional pressure, generating a strong response from civil society and European institutions.
HU.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF, p. 75-81). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Constitutional decision requiring the recognition as a registered partner of certain same-sex marriages held abroad.
Extensive national and international mobilization in defence of Pride and freedom of assembly.
main_challenges: Reverse restrictions on Pride and freedom of assembly and expression.
Restore explicit gender-identity protections and prevent constitutional reforms from eroding the rights of trans, intersex and non-binary persons.

IE.title: Consolidated protections and strong institutional support, with gaps in family, trans healthcare and housing.
IE.summary: Ireland maintains an advanced framework of legal gender recognition and public equality policies, but certain groups remain outside the system and there are gaps in parenthood, trans healthcare and homeless youth.
IE.legal_context: The Gender Recognition Act allows for self-determination for the trans population, although it excludes non-binary persons, under 16 and citizens of Northern Ireland. Organizations claimed full recognition of both parents in LGBTIQ+ families.
IE.social_context: The Government funded dozens of community projects, but long waiting lists and restrictive practices in trans healthcare were documented, as well as disproportionate vulnerability of young LGBTIQ+ to homelessness.
IE.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 83-89 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Financing of €1.7 million for LGBTIQ+ Community services.
Government commitments in security, inclusive education, health, recognition and data.
main_challenges: Reform parental recognition and extend legal gender recognition to groups currently excluded.
Reduce waiting lists in trans healthcare and improve the response to the lack of LGBTIQ+ youth housing.

IS.title: A favourable social and institutional environment, with attention to health and welfare inequalities.
IS.summary: Most people perceive their communities as welcoming for LGBTIQ+ people, although national research continues to detect worse health and welfare indicators than non-LGBTIQ+.
IS.legal_context: The 2025 chapter focuses more on inclusive policies and social data than on major legislative reforms, highlighting inclusive certification of municipal services and LGBTIQ+-sensitive foreign policy.
IS.social_context: A Gallup survey showed a widely positive perception of the local environment, while a research project identified health and welfare inequalities that require specific measures.
IS.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 82-82 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Arcoiris certification of all public pools in Reikiavik and training of staff.
High social perception of reception for LGBTIQ+ people and development of specific research on welfare.
main_challenges: To reduce the health and welfare gaps identified by the research.
Maintain preventive policies against international risks and ensure that inclusion results in health outcomes.

IT.title: Family judicial progress along with a restrictive political climate in education and trans rights.
IT.summary: Courts extended family and parentage rights, but the Government promoted measures and rhetoric against inclusive education, gender-neutral language and access to gender-affirming care for minors.
IT.legal_context: The Constitutional Court extended international adoption to single persons and recognized the filiation of two mothers in certain cases of assisted reproduction, and the Government proposed stricter controls for gender-based treatment in minors.
IT.social_context: Attacks were documented around Pride events and a strong political and religious debate on "gender ideology," inclusive language and sex education.
IT.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 90-93 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: The sentences that extend the rights of adoption and parental recognition in families of two mothers.
Change of documents to use "parents" instead of "father" and "mother" in certain administrative contexts.
main_challenges: Ensure an effective response to anti-LGBTIQ+ violence.
Avoid setbacks in inclusive education and ensure that trans child health policies are based on rights and evidence.

LI.title: Historical progress in marriage equality, with lack of up-to-date data on LGBTIQ+ experiences.
LI.summary: The main change in the report was the entry into force of same-sex marriage; however, an announced government investigation into community living conditions was still pending.
LI.legal_context: Since January 2025, same-sex marriage has been legal following the parliamentary vote of 2024.
LI.social_context: The chapter highlights the lack of a recent public study on the experiences and needs of LGBTIQ+ people in the country.
LI.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 105-105 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: The entry into force of the equal marriage.
Formal consolidation of marriage equality within the national legal framework.
main_challenges: Publish data and studies on living conditions and discrimination against LGBTIQ+ persons.
To assess the practical application of equality beyond marriage recognition.

LT.title: Family judicial progress, with significant gaps in couples and legal gender recognition.
LT.summary: Constitutional jurisprudence has strengthened a gender-neutral family concept, but Parliament has not yet created comprehensive frameworks for same-sex couples or legal gender recognition.
LT.legal_context: After constitutional pronouncements, same-sex couples can seek legal recognition, while a proposal for gender-neutral partnerships is still pending. There is still no comprehensive legislative procedure for legal gender recognition.
LT.social_context: Threats against anti-LGBTIQ+ activists and speeches were documented in political spaces, as well as concerns about the prolonged non-compliance with European obligations.
LT.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 106-108 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Constitutional jurisprudence that recognizes the concept of family as gender neutral.
Presentation of a registered partnership legislative proposal and institutional debate on LGBTIQ+ rights in health.
main_challenges: Adopt a general framework of couples and a procedure for legal recognition of gender.
Protect activists from threats and improve police response to attacks and harassment.

LU.title: A favourable institutional framework, with an ambitious action plan but some shortcomings identified by civil society.
LU.summary: Luxembourg updated its national plan LGBTIQ+ with numerous measures and actions, while human rights organizations noted that medicalized aspects of trans healthcare and recognition persist.
LU.legal_context: The new LGBTIQ+ PAN includes 81 measures and 147 actions in 15 areas. Civil society criticized that it does not fully consider depathologisation of trans identities and maintains the requirement of psychiatric certificate to initiate certain processes.
LU.social_context: There were public gestures of inclusion by religious, political and monarchical institutions, along with social debate on the presence of LGBTIQ+ content in education.
LU.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 109-109 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Update of a comprehensive LGBTIQ+ National Plan.
Increased public and institutional recognition of the LGBTIQ+ community.
main_challenges: To fully depathalize the processes linked to the transition and to review psychiatric requirements.
To implement the national plan in a measurable manner and to maintain inclusive education based on the interest of the student.

LV.title: Partial improvements, but with a low sense of representation and persistence of hatred and violence.
LV.summary: The data collected show that many LGBTIQ+ people avoid being visible for fear of discrimination and exclusion, while marriage, parenthood and security remain community priorities.
LV.legal_context: The legislative and political debate remains open in the area of equality and public symbols; Latvia also participated in European initiatives to defend LGBTIQ+ rights.
LV.social_context: A survey cited in the report indicates low perception of national representation, relevant exposure to hate speech and cases of physical violence.
LV.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 103-104 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Increased availability of data on LGBTIQ+ priorities and experiences.
State participation in European diplomatic actions against setbacks in other countries.
main_challenges: To advance in marriage equality, adoption and parental rights.
Improve police and social response to hate speech and violence to increase confidence in reporting.

MC.title: Community visibility is increasing, but with gaps in the rights of same-sex families.
MC.summary: The report highlights the birth of the first LGBTIQ+ association in the Principality and a political debate on the lack of recognition of the non-biological parent in same-sex families.
MC.legal_context: Legal gaps that may leave the non-biological parent unrecognized in same-sex families remain, and parliamentary representatives called for reforms.
MC.social_context: The creation of Mon'Arc In Ciel Monaco opened a new space of visibility, the fight against isolation and dialogue on inclusion.
MC.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF 114-114). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: The first LGBTIQ+ association of Monaco was established.
Opening of parliamentary debate on the rights of children in same-sex families.
main_challenges: To close the legal vacuum in parental recognition of same-sex families.
Develop public policies and more comprehensive data on the needs of the local LGBTIQ+ community.

MD.title: Polarized environment, with timely institutional protection and strong political pressure against LGBTIQ+.
MD.summary: During 2025, proposals were made to restrict adoption, expression and LGBTIQ+ marches, while police and courts also took part in rights protection proceedings.
MD.legal_context: Opposition groups promoted projects to limit LGBTIQ+ activities, adoption and demonstrations; in Transnistria, proposals for "propaganda" were advanced. At the same time, judicial and equality council decisions supported guarantees against discrimination.
MD.social_context: The anti-LGBTIQ+ political and religious discourse was intense, but the police authorities protected the Chisináu Pride march against counterparties.
MD.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF 112-113). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Police action to allow Pride to be held and to avoid clashes.
Judicial and institutional decisions that supported freedom of expression and protection from discrimination.
main_challenges: Avoid the adoption of "propaganda" rules and restrictions on adoption or assembly.
To combat political and religious hate speech and to consolidate uniform protection throughout the territory.

ME.title: A partially developed legal framework, with implementation delays and episodes of violence.
ME.summary: The country had a law on same-sex couples, but a number of harmonization and implementation measures remained pending five years later; the legal recognition of gender based on self-determination remained unapproved.
ME.legal_context: The institutions reviewed the regulatory harmonization with the Sex Couples Act 2020, while the European Parliament noted delays in the legal gender recognition project.
ME.social_context: Attacks on LGBTIQ+ people were documented in Podgorica and doubts remained about the practical effectiveness of equality standards.
ME.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 115-115 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Institutional review of the implementation of the law of same-sex couples.
Maintaining recognition of the need for a gender identity law based on self-determination.
main_challenges: Complete the implementation of the legislation on couples and non-discrimination.
Adopt legal gender recognition and strengthen the prevention and investigation of anti-LGBTIQ+ violence.

MK.title: A high social hostility environment, with violence against Pride and stagnant legal reforms.
MK.summary: The 2025 chapter is marked by attacks on activists and the LGBTIQ+ support centre, while the reform of legal gender recognition remains blocked.
MK.legal_context: The review points to a long-term suspension of reforms related to legal gender recognition and European recommendations to strengthen the prosecution of hate crimes and speech.
MK.social_context: During the Pride period, there were stone attacks, threats and even an attempt to fire the LGBTIQ+ Support Centre.
MK.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 119-119 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Skopje Pride celebration as a public protest and space of resistance.
The European Parliament called for systematic persecution of hatred and improvements to the Criminal Code.
main_challenges: Unblock legal gender recognition reforms.
To physically protect activists and organizations and effectively pursue violence and hate speech.

MT.title: Very advanced legal framework, but with challenges of violence, social attitudes and full health coverage.
MT.summary: Malta maintains strong institutional recognition and broad legislative development, although the report documents attacks, discriminatory incidents and shortcomings in certain trans healthcare services.
MT.legal_context: The Government highlighted the reforms already adopted - including equal marriage and other rights - and maintained institutional support for equality. Public health care offers several gender-assertive interventions, although not all surgeries are available.
MT.social_context: An organized attack was documented through a dating application and a police incident during the carnival, while services of the Gender Wellbeing Clinic were resumed.
MT.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF 110-111). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Regular resumption of trans / non-binary health services at the Gender Wellbeing Clinic.
The continuation of an institutional and legal framework strongly committed to LGBTIQ+ equality.
main_challenges: Complete the availability of gender-based health care within the public system.
To address violence, prejudice and discriminatory behaviour despite the high level of legal protection.

NL.title: Comprehensive protections, but with increased violence and disputes over asylum and trans rights.
NL.summary: The review shows a consolidated rights environment that is living with an increase in incidents of discrimination and violence, especially in public spaces, reception centres and discussions about policies affecting trans people.
NL.legal_context: The Parliament introduced rules on family reunification in asylum that may affect unmarried couples and the reform of the Transgender Act was discussed, with institutions maintaining instruments of equality and active foreign policy.
NL.social_context: The above-mentioned investigations indicate significant insecurity among LGBTIQ+ asylum-seekers and a sustained increase in reports of violence or discrimination.
NL.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 116-118 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Maintaining active public and diplomatic policies in defence of LGBTIQ+ rights.
Improved availability of data on violence, discrimination and asylum experiences.
main_challenges: Reduce the increase in attacks and discrimination and improve security in shelters.
Ensure that asylum and reforms affecting trans people do not lead to rights setbacks.

NO.title: A favourable institutional environment, with concerns about violence and access to trans healthcare.
NO.summary: Norway maintains public support and inclusion policies, but the report reflects threats against activists, disputes over transgender child health care and persistence of violence.
NO.legal_context: The existing legal recognition of gender continues, while some parties question the introduction of a third category. The State funded police programmes and announced a memorial for the attack on Pride in 2022.
NO.social_context: The possible targeting of activists and protests for restrictions on the health care of young trans was documented.
NO.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF 120-123). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Financing of police training programmes and the creation of a memorial for the 2022 Pride attack.
Strong institutional and foreign policy position in defence of LGBTIQ+ rights.
main_challenges: Ensure accessible, rights-based health care, especially for children.
Prevent violence and threats against activists and Pride events.

PL.title: Improvement over previous years, with judicial progress and the end of the "LGBTIQ+ free zones," although legal gaps remain.
PL.summary: The last local government that maintained a resolution associated with an "LGBTI free zone" revoked it and several courts strengthened protections against hatred and discrimination.
PL.legal_context: Legislation was promoted to expand the grounds protected for hate crimes, although the political process was not fully completed; a framework for the recognition of same-sex couples and reforms for legal gender recognition remained pending.
PL.social_context: The courts had sanctioned homophobic speeches and recognized for the first time discrimination against a non-binary person in employment; anti-LGBTIQ+ campaigns in education and politics were still in place.
PL.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 124-128 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Revocation of the last local resolution associated with an "LGBTIQ+ free zone."
Relevant judicial decisions against hate speech and discrimination, including protection of non-binary persons.
main_challenges: Complete reforms of hate crimes and recognition of same-sex couples.
Reduce political and educational polarization and progress in legal recognition of gender.

PT.title: A significant rights framework, but with violence against trans people and signs of regression in education.
PT.summary: Portugal maintains important legal protections, including the prohibition of conversion practices, although violent attacks and educational decisions were documented that reduce content on sexuality.
PT.legal_context: The prohibition of conversion practices remains in force, but it was noted that its implementation still shows limited progress. The Ministry of Education announced the removal of sexuality and sexual / reproductive health content from the citizenship curriculum.
PT.social_context: Serious attacks were reported against trans women and the mobilization of LGBTIQ+ organizations in the face of far-right initiatives.
PT.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 129-129 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Monitoring of the prohibition of conversion practices and continuity of institutional and civil mobilization for equality.
A comprehensive response from LGBTIQ+ and human rights organizations to extreme right-wing events.
main_challenges: To effectively implement the prohibition of conversion practices.
To strengthen the safety of trans people and to preserve rights-based, inclusive sexual education.

RO.title: Insufficient protection and strong political polarization, with family rights still pending.
RO.summary: The review documents intense anti-LGBTIQ+ rhetoric during the elections and the lack of reforms to legally recognize same-sex couples despite European obligations.
RO.legal_context: A legislative initiative had not been adopted to ensure recognition and protection of same-sex families; the Constitutional Court had also considered issues of access to health insurance for same-sex spouses.
RO.social_context: Political and media discourse often used anti-LGBTIQ+ messages; Pride and civil society maintained mobilization for civil unions, gender recognition and hate protection.
RO.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (pp. 130-131 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Interventions by the audiovisual regulator against discriminatory messages.
Extensive mobilization of civil society in support of Pride and equality reforms.
main_challenges: To fulfil the obligations of legal recognition and protection of same-sex couples.
Reduce political hate speech and move forward in legal recognition of gender and legislation against pretrial crimes.

RS.title: Partial legal framework, with structural discrimination and pressure on civil society.
RS.summary: Serbia recognizes certain rights in asylum and employment, but there is still daily discrimination, hate speech, violence and regulatory threats to organizations.
RS.legal_context: Asylum legislation recognizes persecution for sexual orientation or gender identity, although implementation requires better training; labour protection of gender identity remains indirect and reforms are pending.
RS.social_context: Discrimination in housing and services, hostility of political and religious figures, and attacks around Pride events were documented.
RS.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 137-138 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Legal recognition of SOGI as possible grounds for asylum persecution.
Continuity of Pride and civil work to improve procedures and legislation.
main_challenges: Introduce explicit gender identity protection and improve the implementation of rights in services and employment.
Avoid "foreign agents" rules that restrict civil society and combat anti-LGBTIQ+ speech and violence.

RU.title: Extremely repressive environment, with criminalization and systematic monitoring of the LGBTIQ+ community.
RU.summary: The designation of the so-called "international LGBT movement" as an extremist continued to be used for investigations, censorship, raids and criminal proceedings, while the application of "propaganda" laws was extended.
RU.legal_context: The rules of extremism and "propaganda" severely restrict expression, association and access to content. The ECHR continued to issue resolutions on rights violations, although the internal framework continued to be hardened.
RU.social_context: Organization closures and blockades were documented, raids in queer spaces, convictions for activism or LGBTIQ+ content and police plans for a LGBTIQ+ database.
RU.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF 132-135). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Decisions by international courts continued to document violations and establish standards of protection.
Human rights defenders and networks continued to experience abuses despite high risk.
main_challenges: To end the criminalization under laws of extremism and "propaganda."
Stop surveillance, raids, databases, persecution of activists and restrictions on freedom of association and expression.

SE.title: Strong protections and new policies, with challenges in asylum, intersex rights and the living conditions of trans people.
SE.summary: Sweden strengthened action and funding plans and launched a new gender identity law, although studies show employment vulnerability among trans people and lack of adequate legal protection of intersex bodily integrity.
SE.legal_context: The new Gender Identity Act came into force in July and generated a high initial number of applications. The Government launched a LGBTIQ+ 2024-2027 plan and increased funding for anti-discrimination measures and organizations.
SE.social_context: The data show higher unemployment and economic vulnerability among trans people, along with social concern about the increase in anti-queer attacks.
SE.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 152-155 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: The new law on gender identity is in force.
New LGBTIQ+ action plan and increased public funding for equality and organisations.
main_challenges: To create specific legal guarantees for the rights and bodily integrity of intersex persons.
Improve employment and well-being of trans persons and ensure asylum procedures that are sensitive to the LGBTIQ+ reality.

SI.title: A relatively favourable framework, but with increased hostility and a national strategy for abandoned equality.
SI.summary: Although there are advances in reproductive health and equality policies, 2025 was marked by hostile discourse, violence and the decision to abandon a national LGBTIQ+ strategy under preparation.
SI.legal_context: The Parliament extended access to assisted reproduction in accordance with a constitutional sentence; legal gender recognition does not require medical treatment according to administrative interpretation, but the pending legislative amendment was not completed.
SI.social_context: Organizations documented an increase in stigmatizing narratives, vandalism and attacks, along with cases of discrimination and violence.
SI.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (pp. 142-144 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Reformation of assisted reproduction to meet constitutional standards of equality.
Previous joint work between ministries, NGOs and experts to identify health, education and protection gaps.
main_challenges: To revisit a national LGBTIQ+ equality strategy with clear objectives.
Combat violence and hate speech and complete the legislative reform of legal gender recognition.

SK.title: Significant constitutional backwardness with direct impact on LGBTIQ+ and trans people.
SK.summary: In 2025, constitutional changes were adopted, which recognize only two sexes, restrict adoption and affect gender education and recognition, generating criticism from European and international institutions.
SK.legal_context: The constitutional reforms define sex in binary terms, limit adoption to married heterosexual couples and restrict gender recognition to exceptional situations, and also conflict over the primacy of European law has arisen.
SK.social_context: The anti-LGBTIQ+ political discourse increased and civil organizations warned that hatred was being moved to laws, speeches and public debate.
SK.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (PDF 139-141). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Civil society and multiple international institutions reacted in a coordinated manner to the reforms.
European challenges and procedures maintain external oversight over the deterioration of rights.
main_challenges: Reverse or correct discriminatory constitutional reforms.
Restore effective guarantees for transnationals, same-sex families and inclusive education.

SM.title: Small concrete advances in health, visibility and preparation of legal gender recognition.
SM.summary: The report records new access routes to PrEP, greater public visibility of the community and preliminary institutional work on legal gender recognition and trans healthcare.
SM.legal_context: The health authority prepared procedural guidelines for applications for legal recognition of gender and specific health care, still in the development phase.
SM.social_context: Association 121 participated for the first time officially in Rimini Summer Pride, increasing the visibility of the San Marino community.
SM.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 136-136 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Creation of a structured way to access PrEP through the state hospital.
Development of guidelines for legal recognition of gender and trans healthcare, as well as greater visibility in Pride.
main_challenges: To make preliminary guidelines for gender recognition a clear and fully operational procedure.
Consolidate health services and public policies LGBTIQ+ beyond specific initiatives.

TR.title: Serious backwardness, with government hostility, restrictions on assembly and pressure on organizations.
TR.summary: The Government and senior officials intensified anti-LGBTIQ+ rhetoric, while Pride bans, closures and proceedings against associations, activists and spaces for expression continued.
TR.legal_context: The governments continued to ban Pride acts and courts reviewed some prohibitions; one of them was overturned by a court in İzmir. At the same time, the Young LGBTIQ+ + Association network account was ordered to be closed and proceedings against activists were conducted.
TR.social_context: The official rhetoric presented LGBTIQ+ identities as a threat to the family, while organizations, university clubs and defenders suffered closures, arrests and processes.
TR.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 159-165 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Some court decisions either annulled Pride's prohibitions or acquitted activists.
Civil society maintained community spaces and support networks despite the restrictive context.
main_challenges: Ending the ban on Pride, the persecution of activists and the closure of organizations.
Reduce stigmatizing state rhetoric and guarantee freedom of association, expression and inclusive education.

UA.title: Legislative progress in preparation, in a context of war and persistent anti-LGBTIQ+ violence.
UA.summary: The Government had submitted a reform to strengthen the response to discrimination, crimes and hate speech, and a court had legally recognized a same-sex couple as a family.
UA.legal_context: Bill 13597 incorporates sexual orientation and gender identity into a strengthened framework against discrimination and hate crimes, although it was still pending at the end of 2025. A Kyiv court recognized a same-sex couple as a family.
UA.social_context: Attacks and threats against LGBTIQ+ individuals and activists were documented, with doubts about the speed and proper classification of some incidents by the police.
UA.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (p. 168-170 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: A comprehensive reform against discrimination and hate crimes with SGI protection.
Kyiv's sentence that he recognized a same-sex couple as a family.
main_challenges: Adopt and implement hate crime reform.
Improve police response to anti-LGBTIQ+ attacks and ensure effective protection in the context of war.

XK.title: Visible institutional support, but with violence, underreporting and pending civil-law reforms.
XK.summary: Kosovo showed public support for Pride and recognizes sexual orientation and gender identity as possible grounds for asylum, although practical protection and the Civil Code remain incomplete.
XK.legal_context: The asylum framework provides for persecution for sexual orientation or gender identity, but safeguards and specialized training are lacking.
XK.social_context: Attacks, threats and discrimination in services continued, with strong under-registration for fear of outgoing, retaliation and secondary victimization.
XK.observations: A synthesis prepared for RainbowLens DataHub from the national chapter of ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (pp. 98-98 of the PDF). The 2026 edition documents mainly events that occurred between January and December 2025; the 'general state' is an editorial synthesis and not an official category of ILGA-Europe.
positive_developments: Increased institutional support visible to Pride Week and equality.
First research on experiences that took place during and around the Kosovo war.
main_challenges: Adopt a Civil Code that fully guarantees LGBTIQ+ rights.
Improve violence research, institutional training and confidence to reduce underreporting.
